q1_issues.issue: The comparison is fabricated: "the buck was less aggressive" has an implicit standard (the buck at other times), but the parse asserts (More aggressive sk_group_1 sk_buck_1) — "the other goats were more aggressive than the buck" — a claim the sentence never makes, and it is asserted at top level (factive) as well as sealed.
The same fabricated comparison is what gets sealed under Theme, so the reported content of what Benedito noticed is wrong.

The "when there were other goats around" clause is reduced to a bare (GroupOf sk_group_1 goat) with no relation to the state at all — the temporal/conditional link, the existential predication ("there were … around") and the modifier "other" are all dropped, so the parse loses the sentence's actual claim (a circumstance-dependent change in the buck's aggression).

q2_gaps: a comparative with an elliptical/implicit standard ("was less aggressive", no than-phrase) — More/MoreBy/SameDegree all require two stated arguments
a "when"-clause supplying a circumstance for an INDIVIDUAL's (comparative) state: ConditionalProperty is specified kind-level only, and During requires two reified eventualities

the instruction set is internally inconsistent for exactly this verb: Thematic roles names *notice* in the progressive-test list whose subject is an ordinary Agent, while Propositional attitudes lists *notice* as a factive whose holder is an Experiencer — the parse follows the latter
notes: Name, the projecting definite "the buck" typing, the reified notice event with Past, and the factive seal-plus-assert shape are all correct; the defect is entirely in the complement's content.
